svg.title: Four Gates Before Passing Card Fees to Customers
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-fee-pass-through-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Four Gates Before Passing Card Fees to Customers; subtitle: Compliance checks for surcharging, cash discount, and dual pricing; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is the merchant's effective rate high enough to justify passing the cost on?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stay on standard pricing, since a low effective rate may not be worth passing on.; gate: G2; question: Does the terminal or POS block the fee on every debit card, PIN or signature?; pass next: G3; fail action: Reprogram before launch, because a debit card is a debit card no matter how it is run.; gate: G3; question: Does every price exist twice on shelves, menus, the website, and quotes?; pass next: G4; fail action: Fix signage fast; first fines run $1,000, plus $5,000 if not fixed in about 30 to 45 days.; gate: G4; question: Is any surcharge credit-only, within 3%, with 30 days notice to the acquirer?; pass next: Board the program; fail action: Move to dual pricing; a 3.99% card price on $100,000 needs about 3.84% charged to net the merchant zero.; caption: The posted price, not the program name, decides which rules apply, which is why James Huber and Ryan Anthony rank dual pricing first.; assumptions note: Gate order is editorial; cap levels and customer reaction were disputed among practitioners.; note: Sources include Ryan Anthony, POS Nexus, Global Legal Law Firm, and CCSalesPro.

text.title: Four Gates Before Passing Card Fees to Customers
text.tspan: Four Gates Before Passing Card Fees to Customers

circle.title: gate: G1; question: Is the merchant's effective rate high enough to justify passing the cost on?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stay on standard pricing, since a low effective rate may not be worth passing on.

gate: G2; question: Does the terminal or POS block the fee on every debit card, PIN or signature?; pass next: G3; fail action: Reprogram before launch, because a debit card is a debit card no matter how it is run.

gate: G3; question: Does every price exist twice on shelves, menus, the website, and quotes?; pass next: G4; fail action: Fix signage fast; first fines run $1,000, plus $5,000 if not fixed in about 30 to 45 days.

gate: G4; question: Is any surcharge credit-only, within 3%, with 30 days notice to the acquirer?; pass next: Board the program; fail action: Move to dual pricing; a 3.99% card price on $100,000 needs about 3.84% charged to net the merchant zero.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is editorial; cap levels and customer reaction were disputed among practitioners.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order is editorial; cap levels and customer reaction were disputed among practitioners.

text.title: No relationships supplied; nodes shown as an unconnected register. Connectors encode supplied relationships; node positions are schematic.
